name: Wardrobe & outfits
intro: Where the catalog builds fast and outfits come from your own clothes, and where the AI stylist loops on 3 items and charges without asking.

apps.title: Whering: Your Digital Closet
apps.verdict: A solid wardrobe organizer with an outfit planner and auto-styling feature that genuinely helps you wear more of what you already own, though the auto-suggestions tend to cycle through the same combinations.
apps.loved: Day-by-day planner, clothing catalog, lookbooks, community inspiration, free core features
apps.weak: Outfit suggestions repeat and ignore menswear, no manual sorting within categories, slow loading
apps.whoFor: People who want to get more use out of their existing wardrobe and plan outfits ahead of time

quotes.text: really like the concept of this app! great for planning outfits and tracking what i've worn. however, i think there should be a way to manually sort items and outfits within the categories and also in lookbooks.

apps.title: Indyx: Wardrobe & Outfit App
apps.verdict: One of the best wardrobe organizers out there: it changes how you think about shopping and helps you stop buying things you do not need, but URL-import bugs and a redesigned calendar frustrate power users.
apps.loved: Visual clothing catalog that shifts your shopping mindset, flat-lay feature from try-on photos, style books with a personal stylist
apps.weak: URL importer breaks after the first few uploads, support does not help, new calendar is worse than the old one, paywall keeps expanding
apps.whoFor: Mindful shoppers and anyone who wants to organize their wardrobe and buy less

quotes.text: Ever since they moved the calendar and changed its functionality I find it hard to use the app and my usage has dipped from daily to once a month
I use it daily to take my clothing wears, to ensure I am using my wardrobe fully and not leaning to heavily on certain items.

apps.title: Stylebook
apps.verdict: A mature wardrobe organizer with a decade of history that shines at cataloging and travel packing, but suffers from regressions after updates and poor support for menswear.
apps.loved: Trip packing feature, wear-count and cost-per-use stats, link-based import, reliable sync with responsive support
apps.weak: New updates break editing features that used to work, no male clothing categories, no cloud photo storage by default, AI-powered Switch feature gets colors wrong
apps.whoFor: People who like to analyze and optimize their wardrobe, especially frequent travelers

quotes.text: I started tracking my outfits 700 days ago on Stylebook and haven't missed a day! I find it extremely helpful to have data about what I am wearing and how often, especially the cost-per-wear information.
I've been using this app for years. It's a perfect place to organize my closet and plan my week or pack for trips!

I like this app and find it most useful when I'm packing for trips. One thing that would be a huge game changer in the functionality for me would be if you could build looks just using clothes you have already added to the packing list for a particular trip, directly from the trip.

I like this app a lot but was deterred from using it when I had to get a new phone. I re-downloaded the app thinking all the photos I took would still be stored but it wasn't. Turned out I had to do a cloud back-up. I just wish we can log in and the photos are there.

apps.title: Alta Daily: Digital AI Closet
apps.verdict: An AI stylist that works from photos of your real clothes to help break out of a fashion rut, but it often loops back to the same outfits, freezes, and does not account for context like work versus leisure.
apps.loved: Outfit creation from your own wardrobe, shopping wishlist, personalized email support responses, try-on avatar
apps.weak: Repeats the same outfits, ignores newly added items, freezes and disrupts Wi-Fi, avatar does not accurately represent body shape
apps.whoFor: People who experience decision paralysis getting dressed in the morning and want an outside perspective on their wardrobe

quotes.text: This app version (24 June 2026) runs extremely SLOW on iPad mini. Navigation is totally linear and NOT quick or intuitive at all! You can't drag-n-drop a look, item, or avatar into your closet or edit individual pieces (swap out shoes ) from your saved look or list.

This app only styles the same clothes over and over again and if you get something new, it will never style that individual piece EVER. Very little functionality on sorting looks so it just becomes a giant pile where you can't find anything.

I tried two other apps and numerous clothing delivery services that were not useful at all. I love this app because it gives me ideas of outfits with the things I already own. Can't say enough great things about it.
I love the app for packing and special events! I've found it very helpful and fun to mess around with the different possibilities! It's helped me look at my closet differently!

apps.title: ShopLook - Outfit Maker
apps.verdict: A creative outfit-building tool using a branded clothing catalog with a social community that attracts a younger crowd, but it has been flooded with AI-generated content, NSFW search results, and stability issues.
apps.loved: Large clothing catalog for collages, community with contests, free basic access
apps.weak: AI slop has taken over the feed and contests, search returns NSFW content without clear reason, frequent crashes, password reset does not work
apps.whoFor: Teens and young fashion fans who enjoy creating outfits as collages without managing a real wardrobe

quotes.text: This app was so good a few months ago, now it's completely overrun with ai slop. So many of the challenges are ai, and you have to scroll through so much ugly ai to find cute things. Not as fun or charming now.

apps.title: Weather Fit: Outfit Forecast
apps.verdict: A charming weather-based outfit assistant with a customizable character that clearly shows what to wear given current conditions. The functional minimalism works well, but most useful features are behind a paywall and temperature advice can run warm.
apps.loved: Character design, lock screen widget, quick daily outfit guidance, developer is responsive and fixes issues
apps.weak: Most useful features require a subscription, temperature calibration is sometimes off, age rating is 4+ despite problematic ad banners
apps.whoFor: Anyone who wants a simple, visually appealing daily outfit nudge based on the weather without managing a wardrobe

quotes.text: This is a fun, cheerful way to choose your outfit for the day. No more dressing for sun and getting wet in the rain! You can choose from different styles for each clothing type, and you can customize your character to look like you.

If you really want an idea of what to wear based on the weather, this isn't it. It could be and I wish it was. But the clothing choices are not accurate, and the comfort level adjustments are way off.

apps.title: SimpleCloset: Digital Wardrobe
apps.verdict: A clean, uncluttered wardrobe organizer with no social features that works well for cataloging clothes, but the undisclosed 30-item limit frustrates users who spend time uploading only to hit a wall.
apps.loved: No extraneous social features, export function, simple interface, responsive support
apps.weak: 30-item cap with no prior warning, no cross-device sync, cannot add a second photo per item, one user lost access after purchasing a lifetime subscription
apps.whoFor: People who want a simple, private clothing catalog with no social layer and are willing to pay a modest subscription fee

quotes.text: I think the app is very nice and easy to use but I didn't realize that after 30 items, you have to pay to get premium which is a monthly fee. This was irritating because I spent a lot of my time photographing and organizing the items into certain categories and now that was all a waste of time.

apps.title: GetWardrobe Outfit Planner
apps.verdict: A free wardrobe organizer with decent outfit-creation tools, but the auto-generator is random, ads appear on every screen transition, and the free item limit is lower in practice than advertised.
apps.loved: Up to 100 items free, outfit collage creation, trip planning feature
apps.weak: Ads on every screen transition, auto-generated outfits are random, background removal has bugs, community feed contains inappropriate content
apps.whoFor: New users who want a free digital wardrobe without complex requirements

apps.title: Essembl: Outfit Planner
apps.verdict: A newer outfit planner with a smart camera-based item scanner and a daily outfit rating. It worked well until developers started moving previously free features behind a paywall, triggering a wave of backlash from existing users.
apps.loved: Item scanning with solid recognition, outfit generation was best-in-class according to reviews, archive concept like a visual wardrobe diary
apps.weak: Previously free features moved to paid without warning, dark items on dark backgrounds fail to process, app does not open for some users
apps.whoFor: Younger users who want to keep a visual wardrobe journal and do not mind paying for advanced features

quotes.text: The auto remover needs some fine tuning with some manual adjustments like a regi
The app is really good but I would try to make the camera quality better cause whenever I take pictures it takes some of the things out like the shoe laces but overall it's a good app

I used this app every day and I generated tons of outfits and used it suggestions in outfit check, but since a month ago or something, they changed a lot of the features to be premium only which is dumb because these features were free until now.

apps.title: Outfit Planner Lookscope
apps.verdict: A wardrobe organizer with auto-generated outfits: clean design and easy item adding, but the AI regularly assembles mismatched combinations, you cannot manually pair specific items, and an update broke categories and added a forced subscription screen.
apps.loved: Simple interface, fast photo adding, helps you realize how much clothing you actually have
apps.weak: Cannot manually build an outfit, auto-generation produces absurd combinations, paywall appears on re-entry, crashes after updates
apps.whoFor: People who just want to catalog their clothing and are not expecting accurate AI styling

quotes.text: After spending about 2 hours entering photos and information into the app, I was expecting it all to be worth it later, when I could see the outfits the app compiled, however, I was getting outfits of dresses with athletic shorts, and casual shoes

apps.title: Fits – Outfit Planner & Closet
apps.verdict: An outfit planner with a wardrobe catalog: uploading clothes and building basic collages works fine. The AI recommendations are broken and repeat the same items, ignore preferences, and keep suggesting underwear as a bottom layer.
apps.loved: Fast uploading, unlimited item count, easy browsing of collections, daily outfit diary
apps.weak: AI stylist throws errors or produces nonsensical sets, duplicates items, add button disappears after updates, paywall blocks onboarding
apps.whoFor: People who want to manually build collages from their own wardrobe and are not counting on smart recommendations

quotes.text: This lets you upload limitless amount of articles of clothing. It is easy to use, from reordering your items to building your outfit boards. You have the chance to document the outfit of the day and share it with others on the app. It also loads quickly.

I used to make exactly this for myself on photoshop, so this just shortens the process, which I love! Couple of pointers - make jackets able to be opened (similar to layers option) and make shirts be able to be half-tucked! Allow us to access layers to move them up and down, and a scaler for size wo

apps.title: Outfit Formulas: Closet Maker
apps.verdict: An app built around 'monthly outfit formulas' from your own wardrobe, but it suffers from dated sample styles, weak AI, a hidden price of around $100 per year, and reports of continued charges after cancellation.
apps.loved: Outfit formulas reduce morning stress, OOTD community, helps you rediscover forgotten clothes
apps.weak: Users report charges continuing after cancellation, AI ignores clothes you have added, sample styles feel outdated, price is hidden until the end of onboarding
apps.whoFor: People who want ready-made outfits with minimal morning decisions if a subscription around $100 per year does not deter them

quotes.text: I really wanted this to work for me and I appreciate the free trial. I actually found it pretty insulting when I went to get dressed around 7:20 one morning and I checked the app and it wouldn't give me today's formula. Since I was 'probably already dressed' it kept showing me the next day's formula

I am not on social media or into posting content, so I'm honestly surprised how much I'm enjoying the community feature. It's fun to share and see others' OOTD. It's become a positive little part of my day.

apps.title: Combyne - your perfect Outfit
apps.verdict: A social network for creating looks, not a wardrobe organizer. The creative potential is real, but chronic instability and content moderation failures make the experience unreliable.
apps.loved: Large community, plenty of outfit inspiration, freedom of expression through stickers and collages
apps.weak: App crashes when trying to post a look, ads appear too frequently, accounts get lost, adult content and messages from strangers are not blocked automatically
apps.whoFor: Teens and young adults who want a social platform for sharing outfits rather than tracking a real wardrobe

quotes.text: i love combyne so much!! its definitely my favorite social media platform! you can make outfits with an endless amount of stickers and pics, or post pictures!

Went on the app because I thought it would be fun with all the good reviews... saw several inappropriate posts of people who are clearly not old enough to make those posts. Obviously I reported them but I feel like they should be instantly dealt with if someone is underage

apps.title: Acloset - AI Fashion Assistant
apps.verdict: The wardrobe catalog with wear-tracking and cost-per-wear stats is stable, but the AI recommendations are the main pain point: it suggests winter clothes at 80F, loops on 3 to 4 items out of 80, and smart picks broke after the last update.
apps.loved: Wear stats, cost-per-wear, long-term tracker of what was worn and when, supports all clothing types including workwear
apps.weak: AI ignores weather and repeats the same suggestions, background removal broken on the free tier, crashes on upload, virtual try-on is paywalled
apps.whoFor: Anyone serious about manually logging their wardrobe. Do not count on the AI features

quotes.text: I'm having trouble getting a clean background removal with the free version. Creating outfits is not very fun again because of the messy background removal. I think about the only way this app will work is if I manually edit the images in another program and then import the clean images into this ap

I do find that this app is pretty useful. It takes a minute to upload all your clothes but it does help me keep track of outfits. But the ai is honestly trash. The outfits it recommends me are honestly just horrifying. Every day no matter the water it recommends that same outfits

I've enjoyed using this app so much over the years that I pay for extra closet space. I've used it for years to try to make the list of my closet. I don't necessarily use the outfit suggestions much, but I like the usage statistics, cost per wear, and looking back at what I wear each day.

For 82 F degree weather, this system recommends wool pants, long sleeve pullover sweaters AND cardigans. This would give one the medical malady heat stroke and possibly unalive the wearer. They do this constantly.

apps.title: Fitted
apps.verdict: A young wardrobe organizer app with an interesting concept, but the AI fails to recognize basic items like dresses, the outfit generator is random, and the free limit of 10 items is too low for any practical use.
apps.loved: Helps you see everything in your closet and think about outfit variety, clean interface
apps.weak: AI misclassifies clothing types, outfits come out mismatched, cannot edit item descriptions, 10-item free limit is not enough to be useful
apps.whoFor: Students and younger users who want to organize a wardrobe and are ready to pay for a subscription

quotes.text: I really wanted to like this app, but every time I upload a graphic tee it just cuts the graphic out and gets rid of the tee. It's already time consuming to upload so this was very discouraging and not worth the extra hassle. Unfortunately will be deleting my account
I really like this app and it's very user friendly! I wish that it had an option for adding dresses because I have a lot and there are only the tops and bottoms categories and no full piece options.
The app edits around the clothes very well, and cuts out the background. But paying to have more than 10 item's in your closet is crazy to me.

apps.title: My Best Colors
apps.verdict: A color analysis tool with virtual color draping through the phone screen, which is a genuinely original idea. But the app does not automatically assign you a season and only shows palettes for you to interpret yourself, and the paid content does not live up to expectations.
apps.loved: Virtual color draping through the screen, wide range of palettes including jewelry and makeup, one-time purchase option
apps.weak: No automatic color season result, camera crashes for months on end, custom palettes moved to the website instead of staying in the app, capsule wardrobe feature does not work
apps.whoFor: People who already know their color season and want a palette tool. Beginners without prior color knowledge will not get an answer from this app

quotes.text: doesn't analyze your season and give you a result. You have to figure it out yourself even after a $15 purchase!

I purchased this app with the premium features hoping to finally narrow down my best colors. Instead of telling me my 'season' based on a photograph of my face/hair, I was presented with an overwhelming number of choices that left me confused and not any closer to finding my color matches.

apps.title: Aiuta – AI Stylist
apps.verdict: An AI virtual try-on app where you can see clothing on your own photo. The concept is interesting, but recent updates broke content moderation, subscription terms changed without notice, and there is no way to delete generated photos.
apps.loved: Visual try-on of clothes on your own photo, stylist tips, wide brand selection
apps.weak: Broken moderation flags normal photos, subscription terms changed retroactively, no way to delete your data, weak support
apps.whoFor: Anyone who wants to try clothes virtually before buying if they can tolerate instability and privacy concerns

quotes.text: Simple and fast in usage! I just uploaded a picture of myself to the app and applied the virtual clothes to it and saw how it would look like.
After the recent update there is a censor and It will not process images even though there is no material to be censored. The app has been broken

apps.title: Cladwell: Outfit Planner
apps.verdict: An outfit planner built on the philosophy of wearing what you already own, but the algorithm stubbornly repeats the same combinations, weather data gets stuck on wrong values, support ignores users for years, and reports of charges continuing after cancellation are serious.
apps.loved: Minimalist wardrobe philosophy and day-by-day outfit planning, handy for trips and frequent travel
apps.weak: Algorithm does not learn, weather freezes on incorrect values, categories cannot be corrected after AI processing, several users report charges years after cancellation
apps.whoFor: Minimalists and capsule wardrobe devotees who are willing to accept significant technical and billing risks

quotes.text: The weather feature was a nice touch at first but it has been stuck at 65H/55L every day and recommending outfits with sweaters and cardigans for that range. It is currently 95H and 77L where I live.

apps.title: Smart Closet - Your Stylist
apps.verdict: Once a beloved wardrobe organizer with LookBook support, but after a series of updates Facebook and Gmail login broke and hundreds of users lost years of collected data. Support does not respond to emails.
apps.loved: Built-in browser for importing photos from Google, LookBook collections, category-based organization
apps.weak: Mass data loss during updates, Facebook login broken for over a year, no response from support, no sorting options
apps.whoFor: Not recommended for anyone until login and data integrity issues are fixed

quotes.text: I love this app, but with the most recent update I was signed out and when I signed back in all my accounts data was missing. Where did it go?? I had it backed up to an Apple ID account. My wardrobe entries and outfit collages are gone and I want them recovered!

I love this app and was using it for years. I put in a lot of effort taking pictures of every single clothing piece i own. Then suddenly about a week ago, i got logged out of my account and haven't been able to log back in, therefore losing access to all my closet and outfit combinations.

apps.title: Style DNA: AI Stylist & Closet
apps.verdict: An app centered on color type analysis and style matching, but with predatory monetization: unauthorized recurring charges, two separate cancellation points, and ignored refund requests.
apps.loved: Color analysis helped some users understand which shades work for them
apps.weak: Charges continue after cancellation, support is unreachable (404 error), AI recommendations are repetitive, no way to style your own clothes
apps.whoFor: Not recommended for anyone in its current state due to critical billing issues

quotes.text: people pay BIG BUCKS to get this done in person but i'm so glad i found this app. i had no idea i was wearing the entirely wrong color palette for my skin. now i feel way more confident in every out for :)
I never realized that I was a color girl!! My entire wardrobe consists of neutrals but when style dna suggested a blue, I went for it and omg I could have never guessed how good color looks on me.

apps.title: My Color Analysis・AI StyleLab
apps.verdict: A color analysis and virtual try-on app with body type recommendations. The core idea works, but canceling without an Apple account requires contacting support that does not respond or bounces emails back, and the custom mode is broken.
apps.loved: Silhouette and body type recommendations, variety of clothing styles to try on
apps.weak: Photos load forever, custom AI mode throws errors, no real support channel, unauthorized charges reported by some users, male users get female product suggestions
apps.whoFor: Only with caution and only through an in-app App Store purchase so you can cancel through Apple

apps.title: Pureple: AI Outfit Planner
apps.verdict: A wardrobe organizer that used to support collaborative styling but has degraded into an aggressively monetized product with ads every two clicks and reports of unauthorized charges.
apps.loved: Previously did a good job cataloging wardrobes and enabling collaborative styling
apps.whoFor: Not recommended for anyone: the app is in decline with signs of violations

quotes.text: The ads every 2 seconds is insane but I dealt with it because I've been using this ad for years and I mostly used it for the calendar feature. But now they are making the calendar feature apart of the pro version and making you pay 6.99 A WEEK to use it.

I love Pureple, I've been using it for years. I used AI to create outfits for my recent vacation, selecting items such as jewelry, purses, and shoes. It was amazing and perfect. It really helped me not overpack, for once!

App has potential but there are issues that don't seem to get resolved. Hitting 'Sync All Data' is like a death wish if you want old items you've deleted to reappear all over again vs not syncing across different devices.

apps.title: My Wardrobe - Outfit Closet
apps.verdict: A digital wardrobe concept that breaks almost immediately: background removal crops out clothing, the free item limit of 7 to 9 is hidden until you start using it, there are no outfit recommendations, and developers have not fixed the same issues for years.
apps.loved: Basic idea of cataloging outfits and planning looks, some users praise the speed for school use
apps.weak: Background removal ruins photos, 7 to 9 item limit with no prior warning, no outfit recommendations, cannot create custom categories, outfit calendar has a bug where outfits disappear
apps.whoFor: Practically no one: too little free functionality and too many unresolved issues

quotes.text: I can keep track of my clothes, spending, and clothes age. Would love a feature that lets you know if you wore it yet or not unless there is one and I haven't found it yet.
I really thought this was going to be good until after nine items it says I have to buy the app and it took me 4 hours to do the nine honestly I would just get a different app!

apps.title: Letsy: Try On Outfits with AI
apps.verdict: An AI try-on app with a broken core feature: it systematically ignores color instructions, the server is unavailable 9 times out of 10, and ads show up even on a paid subscription. The product does not match what the promo shows.
apps.loved: Occasionally delivers interesting results with natural poses and simple requests
apps.weak: AI ignores color change commands, server is constantly down, paid subscription does not remove ads, promotional materials are misleading

quotes.text: Works good if the body position is natural, without overlapping parts. Great for trying new colors and styles.
This app is a joke. It can't even change my green pants into blue pants with the simplest possible instruction, 'blue pants'. It seriously only added an ironed in crease and kept the green color.

apps.title: Inspoy: Outfit Maker, Planner
apps.verdict: An app offering style content and color analysis, but real user experience means unauthorized charges after cancellation, support refusing refunds, and no way to unsubscribe from within the app.
apps.loved: Visually pleasant interface, educational style content according to those who read it
apps.weak: Unauthorized recurring charges after cancellation, hidden subscription terms, support ignores refund requests, unsubscription only possible through third-party channels
apps.whoFor: Not recommended for anyone due to documented fraudulent billing practices

apps.title: GRWM - AI Stylist
apps.verdict: An outfit rating app with a lengthy style questionnaire, but all functionality is locked behind a subscription with no actual free mode. Many users cannot even pay because the subscription button freezes.
apps.loved: Stylish onboarding questionnaire about personal style
apps.whoFor: Not recommended in its current state

apps.title: Dressly: AI Outfit Stylist
apps.verdict: An AI stylist with basic tips that profits from an opaque subscription and unauthorized charges. Recommendations ignore stated preferences and links go to SHEIN.
apps.loved: The AI try-on concept is appealing. Basic wardrobe-building educational content is useful to some
apps.weak: Charges happen without authorization and continue after cancellation, no way to reach support, recommends SHEIN despite explicit refusals, ignores stated sizes, recommended items are often out of stock
apps.whoFor: No one: documented unauthorized charges make installing this app a financial risk

apps.title: Closetly - AI Wardrobe Stylist
apps.verdict: Virtual clothing try-on on an avatar, heavily advertised on TikTok. In practice: no real free access, clothing gets cut off awkwardly, item classification is wrong, and subscriptions are taken without a way to cancel from within the app.
apps.loved: Promotional videos look attractive
apps.weak: All functionality is locked behind a paywall from the first second, AI misidentifies clothing type and length, subscription charges without consent, app reportedly does not work even after payment
apps.whoFor: Not recommended for anyone

scenarios.name: Wardrobe collectors
scenarios.job: See the entire closet as one picture, track what gets worn often and what hangs as dead weight, and know the real cost of every item
scenarios.gap: Authors ask for manual sorting and for working with a large catalog. Custom categories, bulk actions and an export of the records all help.

scenarios.name: Capsule wardrobe builders and mindful shoppers
scenarios.job: Stop buying things they do not need, build a capsule wardrobe from what they already own, and get dressed every day without stress
scenarios.gap: Authors describe combinations that repeat. A choice of occasion, excluding an item and taking manual preferences into account all help.

scenarios.name: Travelers packing in their head
scenarios.job: Pack the suitcase in advance, plan outfits for every day of the trip, and not take anything extra
scenarios.gap: Authors want to build outfits only from the suitcase they chose and to hide off-season clothes. That is a specific filtering mode for the catalog.

scenarios.name: Resellers and stylists with clients
scenarios.job: Keep an inventory of their own and other people’s items, find a specific piece fast, and track what is on loan with whom and what is already sold
scenarios.gap: The requests discuss handing items over and exporting data. The hypothesis is an item status, a recipient and an export of the records, and it is worth testing against a real working scenario.
